conflicts.fact: Charge on the iron roof and the explanation of why it was struck versus the wooden stall: free electrons moving through the roof (conduction) versus induction of charge on the roof, and what role the induced charge plays
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 says the iron roof's free electrons let the cloud's charge flow through it, and that the hairs stood up because of an attractive force on opposite charges in the hair. Lesson 1 says hairs stood up because the hairs repelled each other. Lesson 4 says the roof became positive on its upper surface by induction. Lesson 9 says the roof had a deficit of electrons. Lesson 5 explains the strike by the roof's induced charge being closest, via a Coulomb force.

conflicts.fact: Coulomb's Law is taught twice as separate lessons (3 and 5), with the cloud charge and cloud-roof geometry differing
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 uses a cloud 800 m above the Rift Valley Escarpment with a charge separation of 20 C and a discharge triggered by the cloud descending closer. Lesson 5 uses a cumulonimbus cloud over Ol Kalou with up to -40 C and the roof as the closest conductor. Lesson 3's model also shows the cloud base negative with positive induced charge on the roof.

conflicts.fact: Graph shapes and the way the data are analysed for the force-distance relationship; lesson numbering/titles duplicate
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 plots F vs 1/r² giving a straight line through the origin, while Lesson 5 plots F vs r and describes a curved inverse-square relationship. Lessons 3 and 5 share the same title 'How Strong Is the Push or Pull Between Charges?'.

conflicts.fact: Energy stored in the Ol Kalou cloud-ground capacitor and the capacitance/voltage figures, and plates of the capacitor
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 states the energy stored is up to 1.5 × 10⁹ J with an estimated voltage of 300 MV, and sets the cloud-to-ground gap as the capacitor. Lesson 6 describes the capacitor as the cloud base and the iron roof. Lesson 8 says the capacitance is modest, with energy estimated from current and duration data, while Lesson 7 uses 1.5×10⁹ J. Lesson 8 also says Lesson 6's foil capacitor was 470 pF, but Lesson 6 says 200 to 500 pF, and the lessons disagree on the energy figure.

conflicts.fact: Where capacitance and Q=CV are introduced and what voltage the foil capacitor was charged to
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 charges the foil capacitor from a 9 V battery and introduces C = Q/V. Lesson 7 re-introduces C = Q/V and uses 1.5 V, 3 V and 4.5 V. Lesson 6 says the energy calculation is deferred to Lesson 8, while Lesson 7 already teaches E = ½CV².

conflicts.fact: The Observed section of Lesson 8 contains explanation text, and the Athi River precipitator energy is stated inconsistently
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8's 'Observed' says 'We explained…'. The Athi River answer is given as 62 500 J (6.25×10⁴ J) in the explain phase, and the same value in the DQB phase.

conflicts.fact: Mechanism of cloud charging and the number of unanswered DQB questions
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the cloud charge build-up is not yet explained and relies on charge induced by the cloud. Lesson 9 says it forms by friction between ice crystals and water droplets and has the cloud negatively charged. Lesson 9 says all DQB questions are answered; Lesson 9 timing is 7 minutes in the teacher script versus 8 minutes in the learner text.
